newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate quoted at 28/30 pct-dealers.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate quoted at 28/30 pct-dealers.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate in Kuala Lumpur rose sharply on Thursday on an expected liquidity squeeze and after Bank Negara said that it would allow interest rates to rise again, dealers said.
At 0705 GMT, the overnight was quoted at 28/30 percent against 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
Soon after, the rate jumped to 45/50 percent, dealers said.

Dealers said the rise was triggered by sudden tightening of liquidity in the banking system as a result of Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday to help the ringgit.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers said it could mop up anything from 2.5 billion to 5.0 billion ringgit from the system.
Settlement of Tuesday's intervention is on Thursday.
"It's crazy out there. The overnight is going higher and higher, and Bank Negara is not doing anything," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said unlike previously, the central bank was not expected to lend funds to the market this time around.
Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said on Wednesday the central bank would not hesitate to take tough measures, including raising interest rates, to stamp out speculation in the ringgit.
Dealers said the warning also raised concern that Bank Negara would re-impose capital controls to broaden its intervention tools.
They said the overnight rate would remain volatile over the next few days.
Earlier, one-month interbank rate was at 9.0/10.0 percent against 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
Three-month money was at 8.5/9.0 percent against 8.0 percent.

Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell sharply across the board as players continued to liquidate positions due to surging interbank rates in the cash maket, futures dealers said.
At 0800 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down 13 points to 92.19, or an implied yield of 7.81 percent.
The December contract fell 11 to 92.41, or 7.59 percent and March 1998 was down eight to 92.52, or 7.48 percent.
